Who we are
The City of Salisbury is the most progressive council in South Australia, driving growth, jobs, housing and opportunity in the north. With a workforce of over 400 people, we offer the chance to collaborate with teams across the organisation to deliver meaningful, community-focused projects.
The City Infrastructure Department delivers asset management, capital works, and maintenance programs, as well as oversees lease management for local community and sporting clubs, and security and civil compliance functions.
Join us and see the positive impact your work can make.
About the role
The City of Salisbury is seeking three experienced Asset Engineers to join the Engineering Assets & Systems team within City Infrastructure. Opportunities are available across Civil, Roads and Drainage asset portfolios.
Reporting to the Divisional Head, Engineering Assets & Systems (Asset Engineer - Civil and Asset Engineer - Roads) or the Senior Stormwater Engineer (Asset Engineer - Drainage), you will be responsible for developing, maintaining and improving asset management plans, undertaking engineering investigations and modelling, and supporting long-term infrastructure planning and investment decisions.
You will play a key role in managing and improving some of the City's most important infrastructure assets, including roads, drainage networks, wetlands, bridges, boardwalks, coastal assets, carparks, signage and stormwater infrastructure, helping ensure they continue to meet the needs of our growing community.
Your key responsibilities will include
- Develop, maintain and improve Asset Management Plans across a range of infrastructure asset classes.
- Undertake engineering investigations, modelling, analysis and reporting to support asset management decisions.
- Develop capital renewal, maintenance and lifecycle programs.
- Assess asset condition, risk, service levels and long-term investment priorities.
- Prepare project briefs and business cases for infrastructure projects and renewal programs.
- Evaluate consultant reports, designs and technical proposals.
- Provide specialist engineering and asset management advice across the organisation.
- Support planning for future growth and infrastructure needs across the city.
- Build and maintain effective working relationships with community members, developers, government agencies, service authorities and internal stakeholders.
- Communicate technical information and asset management recommendations clearly to a diverse range of stakeholders, including residents, elected members and senior leaders.
- Respond to enquiries from residents, elected members and other stakeholders.
About you
You are a qualified engineer with experience in infrastructure asset management and a passion for delivering practical, long-term outcomes for communities. You combine strong technical capability with excellent communication skills and can confidently engage with a wide range of stakeholders. You are able to translate complex engineering and asset management information into clear, practical advice that supports informed decision-making.
You will also have
- Degree qualifications in Civil Engineering, equivalent qualifications, or proven extensive experience in asset management relating to civil infrastructure and stormwater.
- Experience in infrastructure asset management, planning and lifecycle analysis.
- Knowledge of asset management frameworks such as ISO 55000 and IIMM/IPWEA practices.
- Experience using asset management, GIS and engineering modelling systems.
- Demonstrated ability to communicate technical information to both technical and non-technical audiences.
- Proven experience building productive relationships with a diverse range of internal and external stakeholders.
- Strong written communication skills, including the preparation of reports, business cases and technical documentation.
- Strong analytical, problem-solving and decision-making skills.
- Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities.
- Current driver's licence.
Desirable
- Postgraduate qualifications in asset management.
- Experience working within local government.
What we offer
- State-of-the-art Salisbury Community Hub is 25 minutes from the CBD with excellent rail and road connections.
- Modern and positive work environments.
- Free car parking.
- Flexible work options.
- Three additional leave days per year.
- Annual pay rises.
- Health and wellbeing programs, including skin checks, health assessments, flu vaccinations and an employee assistance program.
- Professional development opportunities.

We are committed to creating a safe, inclusive and diverse workplace where everyone feels valued and respected. We encourage applications from people of all backgrounds and experiences, including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, people from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds, people with disability, veterans, and members of the LGBTQIA+ community.

Company Overview
Noble Built is an Adelaide-based residential construction and property development company specialising in custom home design and construction, residential property development, knockdown and rebuild projects, land subdivision and investment builds. The Company provides comprehensive project services, from initial feasibility assessments, design and council approvals through to construction and final handover. With a focus on quality workmanship, functional design, cost-effective solutions and effective project delivery, Noble Built works with homeowners, landowners and investors to deliver tailored residential projects across Adelaide, South Australia.
About the role
Noble Built is seeking a skilled and experienced Civil Engineering Draftsperson to join our team in Adelaide, South Australia. The successful candidate will be responsible for preparing, developing and modifying detailed civil engineering drawings and technical documentation for residential construction and property development projects. Working closely with project management team, the role will involve preparing engineering drawings based on design requirements and technical specifications, incorporating drawing revisions and ensuring documentation complies with relevant Australian Standards, building codes and local council requirements. This position will play an important role in supporting the preparation of civil engineering documentation and the delivery of the Company's residential projects.
Key Responsibilities
1.           Assisting civil engineer and project supervisor in preparing civil engineering drawings and technical documentation for residential construction, property development and land subdivision projects.
2.           Preparing detailed civil engineering drawings for site layouts, earthworks, site grading, stormwater drainage, sewerage, water supply and associated civil infrastructure works.
3.           Preparing, developing and modifying engineering drawings, sketches and plans in accordance with engineering designs, technical specifications and project requirements.
4.           Preparing technical specifications, drawing schedules and supporting documentation for civil engineering works.
5.           Reviewing survey plans, site measurements and engineering information to ensure the accuracy and completeness of civil engineering drawings.
6.           Using computer-aided design software, including AutoCAD and Civil 3D, to produce, update and revise detailed engineering drawings.
7.           Conducting site inspections, where required, to verify site conditions and identify discrepancies between engineering drawings and actual site conditions.

candidates.content_text:
The UGL Utilities team designs, constructs and maintains critical infrastructure across the water and power sectors. Ranging from wastewater treatment plants to power stations. We design and construct the following assets; power generation, transmission lines, substations, electrical distribution networks, water and wastewater treatment plans and water pipelines.
 Our Utilities team works hard and celebrates successes and efforts. If you are looking for a bright future and opportunity to grow your career, then join UGL – a great place to work!
 The Opportunity
 UGL Utilities team are currently looking for an experienced Civil Project Engineer to join the team in Perth. This role requires DIDO to the project site in Narrogin on a 2:1 roster.  
 Key Responsibilities 
 - Develop and implement detailed project plans, work schedules, and methodologies for civil works, ensuring alignment with project timelines, budgets and scope.
 - Review and interpret technical drawings, specifications, and contracts; provide engineering input to ensure compliance with industry standards, UGL requirements, and client expectations.
 - Oversee on-site civil construction activities, ensuring work is completed safely, efficiently, and to the requires quality standards; manage subcontractor performance and resolve site issues as they arise.
 - Promote and enforce UGL’s HSE policies and procedures across all civil project activities; ensure risk assessments and safety measures are effectively implemented.
 - Liase with clients, internal teams, and external stakeholders to provide regular updates. Manage expectations, and address engineering or construction challenges; prepare and deliver progress reports and technical documentation.
 About you
 - Tertiary qualification in Civil Engineering or a related discipline, with eligibility for membership with Engineers Australia (or equivalent).
 - Proven experience delivering civil engineering works in infrastructure, utilities, or construction projects – ideally within a multi-disciplinary or contractor environment.
 - Strong understanding of civil design principles, construction methodologies, and relevant Australian standards, with the ability to interpret drawings and technical documentation.
 - Demonstrated commitment to health, safety, environmental, and quality standards, with experience implementing and maintaining compliance on project sites.
 - Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to engage confidently with internal teams, client and subcontractors to achieve project outcomes.
 What makes you right for UGL 
 - Ability to provide a safe, supportive, and positive workplace. 
 - Empower a united and collaborative culture.
 - Deliver technical excellence and create efficient, innovative solutions.
 - Build an enviable reputation and the trust of employees, clients, and other stakeholders.
 - Genuine concern for safety.
 About Us   
 UGL is well-known and respected for providing end-to-end engineering, construction and maintenance services within, rai and transport, communications and technology systems, oil and gas, power, renewables and resources, water and defence markets. UGL partners with some of the world’s largest blue-chip companies and government agencies, private enterprises, and public institutions. We are a member of the CIMIC Group of companies.
 At UGL, we value diversity – in the backgrounds, ideas, work styles and perspectives of our team. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and strongly encourage people with disability, Aboriginal & Torres Strait Islander people, mature aged workers, and people from culturally diverse backgrounds to apply. 
 Please note that relevant screening checks will be conducted as part of the recruitment process. These may include a national criminal history check and for you to undergo pre-employment medical assessment including drug and alcohol screen. 
 UGL does not accept unsolicited resumes from recruiters or recruitment agencies.

candidates.content_text:
My client is seeking an experienced Civil Project Engineer to join the project team delivering works on the Pilbara Port of Ashburton Foundations and Firewater Installation Project.
 This is an excellent opportunity for a Civil Project Engineer to secure an immediate start on a three-month FIFO contract, contributing to the delivery of a range of civil infrastructure, foundations and services installation packages.
 The successful candidate will play an integral role in coordinating construction activities, managing subcontractors and ensuring project works are delivered safely, efficiently and in accordance with programme, budget and quality requirements.
On Offer
 - Role: Civil Project Engineer
 - Project: Pilbara Port of Ashburton – Foundations and Firewater Installation
 - Location: Onslow, Western Australia
 - Duration: 3 months
 - Start Date: Immediate 
 - Rate: $87 per hour + superannuation
 - Payment: Weekly
 - Roster: 2:1 FIFO from Perth
 - Hours: 12 hours per day
 - Shift: 6:00am – 6:00pm
 - Flights: Friday afternoon departures from Perth
 Project Scope 
The successful candidate will be involved in the coordination and delivery of multiple civil construction and infrastructure packages, including:
 - Stormwater drainage installation and associated underground services.
 - Coordination and management of in-situ services.
 - Firewater and potable water pipeline installation.
 - Electrical services trenching and installation.
 - Tank foundations and associated infrastructure installation.
 - Soft and hard landscaping works.
 - Road construction and associated civil infrastructure.
 - General earthworks, concrete and foundation works.
 Key Responsibilities 
Reporting to the Project Manager and working closely with the site construction team, your responsibilities will include:
 - Coordinating and managing day-to-day civil construction activities across multiple work fronts.
 - Planning and overseeing the delivery of civil infrastructure, earthworks, concrete, foundations and underground services packages.
 - Managing subcontractors, suppliers, labour resources and plant to ensure works are completed safely and efficiently.
 - Developing and maintaining construction programmes, short-term lookaheads and daily work plans.
 - Monitoring construction progress against project milestones, identifying potential delays and implementing corrective actions.
 - Reviewing and interpreting construction drawings, technical specifications, scopes of work and engineering documentation.
 - Coordinating the installation of stormwater drainage, firewater, potable water and electrical services.
 - Overseeing quality assurance activities, including ITPs, inspections, test records and quality documentation.
 - Ensuring construction activities comply with project specifications, approved methodologies and relevant Australian Standards.
 - Monitoring project costs, variations, productivity and resource utilisation.
 Skills & Experience 
To be considered for this opportunity, you will ideally demonstrate:
 - A minimum of 5 years' experience in civil construction project engineering and delivery.
 - A Bachelor of Engineering (Civil) – mandatory.
 - Strong practical knowledge of concrete, foundations, earthworks and general civil construction.
 - Demonstrated experience coordinating civil infrastructure and underground services installation.
 - Previous experience managing subcontractors and coordinating multiple construction work fronts.
 - The ability to interpret engineering drawings, specifications and construction documentation.
 - Experience with quality assurance processes, ITPs, inspections and project reporting.
 - Strong communication, planning and organisational skills.
 - The ability to work autonomously in a remote construction environment and contribute effectively to the wider project team.
 Mandatory Requirements 
Candidates must hold or be able to provide:
 - Bachelor of Engineering (Civil).
 - Current White Card.
 - Current driver's licence.
 - Australian working rights.
 - Ability to provide 100 points of identification.
 - Current National Police Clearance.
 Apply Now
If you are an experienced Civil Project Engineer with a strong background in civil infrastructure, concrete, foundations and services installation, and are available for an immediate start, we would like to hear from you.

candidates.content_text:
About Us
 For more than 40 years, Residential Engineering has delivered practical engineering solutions to the residential construction industry across New South Wales. Our expertise spans structural and geotechnical engineering, inspections, surveying, and bespoke design services. With a focus on buildable, cost-effective outcomes, we combine responsive service with long-standing client relationships to help deliver successful residential projects with confidence. 
 Residential Engineering is backed by Five Group, a national network of engineering, surveying, consulting, and professional services businesses. Through this connection, we benefit from shared expertise, strong operational support, and a collaborative network that strengthens our capability and creates opportunities for our people and clients across Australia and South-East Asia. 
 Location: Canberra, ACT OR Goulburn, NSW (Field-based & remote)
 Our Benefits
 - Competitive salary package
 - Remote working flexibility with autonomy in your day-to-day role
 - Supportive and close-knit team environment
 - Exposure to a variety of residential construction projects
 - Ongoing training and professional development opportunities
 - Employee Assistance Program and wellbeing initiatives
 Your Role
 As our Structural Site Engineer, you'll play a key role supporting residential construction projects across your region through site inspections, technical assessments and engineering advice.
 This is a predominantly field-based position suited to an engineer who enjoys being out on site, engaging with builders and contractors, and seeing projects firsthand. While inspections will make up majority of your workload, you'll also have opportunities to complete structural design work and technical engineering tasks during quieter periods.
 You'll operate with a high degree of autonomy, planning your inspection schedule, liaising directly with site contacts and delivering practical engineering solutions that support safe and compliant construction outcomes.
 What You’ll Do:
 - Conduct structural inspections across residential construction projects.
 - Plan and manage daily inspection schedules and travel efficiently across your region.
 - Prepare and submit inspection outcomes, photographs and supporting documentation.
 - Liaise with builders, site supervisors and project stakeholders regarding inspection findings.
 - Provide practical engineering advice and recommendations relating to site compliance and construction outcomes.
 - Assist with structural design work, including concrete, steel and timber structures, when inspection workloads permit.
 What You’ll Bring
 - Tertiary qualifications in Civil or Structural Engineering.
 - Training in Asbestos and Silica awareness would be ideal.
 - Experience undertaking site inspections within the Australian construction industry.
 - Working knowledge of residential construction practices and relevant Australian Standards.
 - Exposure to the design of concrete, steel or timber structures.
 - Strong communication skills and the ability to engage confidently with site personnel and clients.
 - Current driver's licence and willingness to travel extensively throughout your allocated region.
 WE ENCOURAGE YOU TO APPLY
 We encourage you to apply and become part of a team where your contribution is valued and your career can grow. At Five Group, we're committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace where people can thrive and succeed. Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted as we progress through the selection process. 
 Recruitment agencies: our Talent Acquisition team recruits directly and will contact selected partners if external support is required.
